hook: A busy little office full of things to find: tap each object in the picture, then give it its article.
intro: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one small, slightly cluttered office with 32 things to find in it, every one a noun you need when you talk about your working day — der Drucker, die Tastatur, das Whiteboard, der Klebebandabroller on the desk. The prompt asks Wo ist der Papierkorb? and you tap it in the picture. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. Once you have passed a run, the hunt turns harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Papierkorb?), and after the find you choose der, die or das yourself. A tap on bare wall costs nothing; a tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking, and after three misses the right one is shown. No object is asked twice in the same run.
tips[0].title: Compounds in the office: the last part decides
tips[0].text: Office words are full of compounds, and only the last part decides the article. Schreibtisch + Lampe: die Lampe, so die Schreibtischlampe. Papier + Korb: der Korb, so der Papierkorb. Notiz + Buch: das Buch, so das Notizbuch.
tips[0].check.why: The last part is der Rechner, so the whole word is der Taschenrechner.
tips[1].title: Machines in -er are masculine — machines in -e are not
tips[1].text: A thing that does a job, named with -er, is masculine: der Drucker, der Ordner, der Taschenrechner, der Klebebandabroller. The ending decides, not the idea of a machine: when the last part ends in -e, the -e rule wins and the word is feminine: die Kaffeemaschine, die Klimaanlage.
tips[1].check.why: It is a machine, but the last part is die Anlage, ending in -e: die Klimaanlage.
tips[2].title: English office words are usually das
tips[2].text: German borrows a lot of office English, and most of these loanwords for things become neuter: das Headset, das Whiteboard, das Sideboard, das Handy. When an English thing turns up in a German office and you are unsure, das is the best first guess. The label colours help: blue der, red die, green das.
tips[2].check.why: Most English loanwords for things become neuter in German: das Headset, das Handy, das Whiteboard.
remember[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: der Schreibtisch + die Lampe → die Schreibtischlampe.
remember[1]: Machines in -er are der (der Drucker, der Ordner); machines in -e are die (die Kaffeemaschine).
remember[2]: English loanwords for things are mostly das: das Headset, das Whiteboard, das Handy.
